directive.exactQuestion: Do the four highest-priority Resolver routes contain materially new contradictions requiring another adjudication, or are they unchanged/resolved dispositions that deterministic reconciliation has failed to consume?
directive.whyItMatters: Resolver owns genuine contradictions, not repeated downstream symptoms. Re-adjudicating unchanged resolved tensions wastes scarce capacity and violates anti-repeat.
directive.preferredEvidencePath: Current deep-resolver routing queue plus the latest immutable Resolver disposition for each work item.
lawfulFallbacks: new primary evidence that conflicts with the existing disposition
directive.successCondition: Classify each route as resolved, unavailable, or still_conflicted and identify the precise next owner/path without weakening any T0 gate.

items.finding: The growth-versus-margin tension remains explicitly non-gating and unchanged. No new conflicting evidence is present in the current route.

items.changedStrategy: consume the existing Resolver disposition in deterministic reconciliation; keep Alpha-owned underwriting/provenance failures with Council Alpha

gateImpact: Resolver contradiction dispositions may clear only their own contradiction labels on reconciliation. No canonical methodology, score, rank, tick, membership, Chief decision, or Alpha/Beta-owned failure is modified.
recommendedDisposition: Deterministic reconciliation should consume immutable Resolver dispositions and suppress unchanged reroutes until inputSignature changes or Chief explicitly adjudicates.
